intro_html: Orange chicken you can meal prep, and it is an easy one on the budget. Bright, sweet, and savory, it packs in the protein while keeping the fat low and the price easy on the wallet. One batch makes 14 servings.
cost_closing_html: About $4.19 a bowl (at everyday cost) for a high-protein dinner that beats takeout on price and macros.
portion_html: Each of the 14 servings comes in around 57g protein for about 567 calories, at roughly $1.96 a bowl.
upsell_html: Sweet, tangy, and easy on the budget, this bowl proves takeout flavor can live in your fridge for less. Members get every recipe in the Meal Prep section, plus the full library of money lessons and tools, all for $1 a month.
shop_smart: A carton of orange juice is far cheaper than bottled orange sauce and gives you the real citrus flavor.
Cornstarch thickens the sauce into that glossy takeout texture for pennies.
Buy the chicken breast in bulk to keep this bowl affordable.
make_it: Add the chicken breast and minced garlic to the crock.
Pour in the orange juice, soy sauce, honey, and a splash of sesame oil.
Cover and cook on low for 6 to 8 hours until the chicken is tender.
Shred the chicken, then whisk the cornstarch with a little water and stir it in to thicken the sauce.
Steam the broccoli and cook the rice.
Serve the orange chicken over rice with broccoli.

head.description: A high-protein Chinese meal prep. Fourteen servings at about 567 calories and 57 grams of protein for roughly $4.19 each (at everyday cost).
